thesis: Hold. Today's three macro items all point at my book and all three are descriptions of price rather than statements of fact, which is the distinction I have been trading on for two weeks. Nasdaq futures are sliding as 'AI warnings' rattle markets with Nvidia and other chip stocks retreating, but the pack never says what the warnings are, who issued them or what they claim; silver is sliding as rate-hike expectations grow, which is a commodity column inferring a rates path from a commodity price; and European shares are muted as tech slides and the oil surge weighs. Strip out the market moves and there is no new fact underneath any of them. I understand the pull here, because all three lean the same way against a book that is roughly 39% NVDA and 80% long-duration tech, and cutting NVDA again this morning would feel prudent. But I trimmed NVDA on 9/8 and wrote then that if every day's continuation justified another cut, I would be running a momentum trade dressed as risk management. An unspecified warning plus a futures print is weaker evidence than the U.S.-Iran escalation I acted on, not stronger, and selling into it is the same tape-trading I refused when futures were rising on 6/9 and when they were falling on 9/8. Consistency has to cut both ways or it is not a rule. The AI-skeptic thread running through the pack is real but it is entirely opinion: a 760 billion dollar AI risk column, a Google and Microsoft veteran on AGI hype, and the UBS CEO calling investors complacent. Opinions from credible people are still opinions, and I declined the bullish version of this exact format when the 89 billion dollar Nvidia column pointed the other way. The rest is Jim Cramer on eight separate tickers, a prediction about Nvidia overtaking Apple on buybacks, a promotional AMD CFO headline for a name outside my universe, and FX and dividend filler. I also note the EUR/USD piece references a Fed decision ahead; as with CPI last week, I will not position for a scheduled event whose outcome I cannot know. The book stands at 4 of 8 positions, NVDA near 39% inside the 50% cap, XOM near 13%, and cash at roughly 7% against the 5% floor, which leaves me little room to act even if today's items had justified it.
